units.zh: 電報之法，自英吉利人初設於其國都，推及於印度，再及於上海。
units.en: Telegraphy was first introduced by the British in their capital, then spread to India, and from there reached Shanghai.
units.literal: The method of telegraphy was first established by the English in their national capital, extended to India, and then extended to Shanghai.

units.zh: 同治十三年，日本犯台灣，兩江總督沈葆楨疏言電報之利，詔旨飭辦，不果行。
units.en: In 1874, when Japan invaded Taiwan, Shen Baozhen, Governor-General of Liangjiang, submitted a memorial on the advantages of telegraphy. The court ordered action, but the plan never went forward.
units.literal: In the thirteenth year of Tongzhi, Japan invaded Taiwan. The Governor-General of Liangjiang Shen Baozhen memorialized on the benefits of telegraphy. An imperial edict ordered it to be carried out, but it was not implemented.

units.zh: 光緒五年，直隸總督李鴻章始於大沽、北塘海口砲台設線達天津，試行之而利，明年因有安設南北洋電報之請。
units.en: In 1879, Li Hongzhang, Governor-General of Zhili, ran telegraph lines from the Dagu and Beitang coastal batteries to Tianjin. The trial proved successful, and the next year he petitioned to establish a telegraph network connecting the northern and southern coasts.
units.literal: In the fifth year of Guangxu, Li Hongzhang, Governor-General of Zhili, first installed lines from the Dagu and Beitang coastal fort batteries to Tianjin. The trial proved beneficial, and the following year a request was made to install telegraphs linking the Northern and Southern Seas.

units.zh: 先是同治間，英使阿禮國請設電線於中國境內，力拒之，乃已。
units.en: Earlier, during the Tongzhi era, the British minister Alcock had asked to lay telegraph lines inside China. The request was firmly refused and dropped.
units.literal: Previously, during the Tongzhi reign, the British envoy Alcock requested to install telegraph lines within Chinese territory. It was firmly rejected and thus ceased.

units.zh: 九年，其使臣威妥瑪復申前議，易陸線為水線，自廣州經閩、浙以達上海，爭之數月，卒如所請。
units.en: In the ninth year [of Tongzhi, 1870], Wade revived the proposal, substituting submarine cables for land lines running from Guangzhou through Fujian and Zhejiang to Shanghai. After months of negotiation, the request was finally approved.
units.literal: In the ninth year, the envoy Wade again raised the earlier proposal, changing land lines to submarine cables from Guangzhou through Fujian and Zhejiang to Shanghai. After disputing for several months, it was ultimately granted as requested.

units.zh: 嗣是香港海線循廣州達天津，陸線達九龍。
units.en: Hong Kong's submarine cable then ran via Guangzhou to Tianjin, while its land line reached Kowloon.
units.literal: Subsequently, Hong Kong's submarine cable ran along Guangzhou to Tianjin, and its land line reached Kowloon.

units.zh: 而丹國陸線亦由吳淞至滬上，駸駸有闌入內地之勢。
units.en: Denmark's land line from Wusong to Shanghai, meanwhile, was steadily pushing inward toward the interior.
units.literal: Meanwhile, Denmark's land line also ran from Wusong to Shanghai, gradually showing a tendency to encroach into the interior.

units.zh: 天津道盛宣懷言於鴻章：「宜仿輪船招商之例，醵集商股，速設津滬陸線，以通南北兩洋之郵，遏外線潛侵之患；
units.en: Sheng Xuanhuai, intendant of Tianjin, told Li Hongzhang: "We should follow the China Merchants Steam Navigation model, raise capital from merchants, and quickly build a land line between Tianjin and Shanghai to link the northern and southern coasts and forestall foreign lines creeping inland;
units.literal: The Tianjin intendant Sheng Xuanhuai said to Li Hongzhang: "One should follow the precedent of the China Merchants Steam Navigation Company, gather merchant shares, and quickly install the Tianjin-Shanghai land line to connect the postal communications of the Northern and Southern Seas and check the danger of foreign lines encroaching in secret;

units.zh: 並設電報學堂，育人才，備任使。」
units.en: and establish a telegraph school to train personnel for future service."
units.literal: and also establish a telegraph academy to cultivate talent and prepare personnel for service."

units.zh: 鴻章韙之。
units.en: Li Hongzhang agreed.
units.literal: Li Hongzhang approved of this.

units.zh: 明年，疏言：「用兵之道，神速為貴。
units.en: The next year he submitted a memorial: "In warfare, speed is paramount.
units.literal: The following year, he memorialized, saying: "In the art of war, speed is prized above all.

units.zh: 泰東西各國於講求槍砲之外，水路則有快輪船，陸路則有火輪車，而數萬里海洋欲通軍信，則又有電報之法。
units.en: Beyond the study of rifles and cannon, the countries of East and West use fast steamships on waterways and steam locomotives on land; to relay military messages across oceans tens of thousands of li wide, they rely on the telegraph.
units.literal: Beyond developing firearms and cannon, the countries of East and West have fast steamships on water routes and steam locomotives on land routes, and for transmitting military communications across tens of thousands of li of ocean, there is also the method of telegraphy.

units.zh: 近來俄羅斯、日本均效而行之。
units.en: Russia and Japan have recently adopted the same practice.
units.literal: Recently Russia and Japan have both followed suit in implementing it.

units.zh: 故由各國以至上海，莫不設立電報，瞬息之間，可以互相問答。
units.en: Every foreign power now maintains telegraph links to Shanghai, exchanging messages in moments.
units.literal: Therefore from every country to Shanghai, telegraphs have been established without exception, and within an instant messages can be exchanged back and forth.

units.zh: 獨中國文書尚恃驛遞，雖日行六百里加緊，亦已遲速懸殊。
units.en: China alone still depends on the postal relay system. Even its fastest couriers, at six hundred li a day, lag hopelessly behind.
units.literal: China alone still relies on courier relay for documents. Even with the six-hundred-li-per-day urgent dispatch, the difference in speed is already vast.

units.zh: 查俄國海線可達上海，旱線可達恰克圖。
units.en: Russia's submarine cable reaches Shanghai, and its land line reaches Kyakhta.
units.literal: It is found that Russia's submarine cable can reach Shanghai, and its land line can reach Kyakhta.

units.zh: 欽使曾紀澤由俄國電報到上海，祗須一日。
units.en: When Imperial Commissioner Zeng Jize sent a telegram from Russia to Shanghai, it took only one day.
units.literal: When the imperial envoy Zeng Jize telegraphed from Russia to Shanghai, it required only one day.

units.zh: 而由上海至京城，輪船附寄，尚須六七日到京。
units.en: Yet a message from Shanghai to the capital, sent by steamship mail, still needed six or seven days to reach Beijing.
units.literal: Yet from Shanghai to the capital, even by steamship mail, six or seven days were still required to reach Beijing.

units.zh: 如遇海道不通，由驛必以十日為期。
units.en: If the sea route were cut off, the relay post would take at least ten days.
units.literal: If the sea route was blocked, relay post would require ten days at minimum.

units.zh: 是上海至京僅二千數百里，較之俄國至上海數萬里，消息反遲十倍。
units.en: Shanghai to the capital is only a few thousand li, yet news travels ten times slower than from Russia to Shanghai, a distance of tens of thousands of li.
units.literal: Thus from Shanghai to the capital is only a few thousand li, yet compared with Russia to Shanghai at tens of thousands of li, news arrives ten times slower.

units.zh: 倘遇用兵之際，彼等外國軍信速於中國，利害已判若徑庭。
units.en: In wartime, foreign powers would relay military intelligence far faster than China—a disparity that could prove decisive.
units.literal: If war should arise, foreign military communications would be faster than China's, and the difference in advantage and harm would already be as far apart as if on different paths.

units.zh: 且其鐵甲兵船，在海洋日行千餘里，勢必聲東擊西，莫可測度，全賴軍報神速，相機調援，是電報實為防務所必需。
units.en: Their ironclads can cover a thousand li a day at sea, striking unpredictably in every direction. Rapid military dispatches are essential to coordinate reinforcements—telegraphy is indispensable to coastal defense.
units.literal: Moreover, their ironclad warships can travel over a thousand li per day on the ocean and will surely feint east while striking west in unpredictable ways. All depends on rapid military reports to adjust reinforcements as circumstances require. Thus telegraphy is truly indispensable to coastal defense.

units.zh: 現自北洋以至南洋，調兵饋餉，在在俱關緊要，亟宜設立電報，以通氣脈。
units.en: From the northern to the southern coast, troop movements and supply lines are everywhere critical. Telegraph lines must be built at once to keep communications open.
units.literal: At present from the Northern Sea to the Southern Sea, deploying troops and supplying provisions are everywhere matters of urgent importance. Telegraphs should be established at once to connect the vital channels of communication.

units.zh: 如由天津陸路循運河以至江北，越長江以達上海，安置旱線，即與外國通中國之電線相接，需費不過十餘萬兩，一半年可以告成。
units.en: A land line from Tianjin along the Grand Canal to the north bank of the Yangtze, then across the river to Shanghai, would link up with foreign telegraph lines entering China. The cost would be under 150,000 taels, and the work could be finished in eighteen months.
units.literal: If a land line were laid from Tianjin along the Grand Canal to north of the Yangtze, crossing the Yangtze to reach Shanghai, it would connect with the foreign telegraph lines entering China. The cost would be no more than a hundred thousand taels, and it could be completed in a year and a half.

units.zh: 約計正線支線，橫亙三千餘里，沿路分設局棧，常年用費，先于軍餉內墊辦。
units.en: Main and branch lines together would span over three thousand li, with offices established along the way. Operating costs would initially be covered from military appropriations.
units.literal: Counting main lines and branch lines together, they would span more than three thousand li. Telegraph offices would be established along the route. Regular operating expenses would first be advanced from military funds.

units.zh: 辦成後，仿照輪船招商章程，擇公正商董，招股集貲，俾令分年繳還本銀。
units.en: Once built, following the China Merchants model, reputable merchant directors would raise capital through share subscriptions, repaying the principal in installments over successive years.
units.literal: After completion, following the China Merchants Steam Navigation regulations, upright merchant directors would be selected to raise capital by selling shares, allowing the principal to be repaid in installments over successive years.

units.zh: 嗣後即由官督商辦，並設電報學堂，僱用洋人教習中國學生，自行經理，庶幾權自我操，歷久不敝。」
units.en: Thereafter the enterprise would be government-supervised and merchant-operated. A telegraph school would train Chinese students under foreign instructors so that operations could be managed independently—keeping control in our hands for the long term."
units.literal: Thereafter it would be government-supervised and merchant-operated. A telegraph academy would also be established, employing Westerners to instruct Chinese students so that management would be handled independently. Thus authority would remain in our hands and endure without decline over time."

units.zh: 疏入，報可。
units.en: The memorial was submitted and approved.
units.literal: The memorial was submitted and approved.

units.zh: 逾年，工竣，以宣懷董其事。
units.en: A year later the project was finished, with Sheng Xuanhuai placed in charge.
units.literal: More than a year later, the work was completed, and Sheng Xuanhuai was put in charge of the undertaking.

units.zh: 未幾，英、法、德、美各使擬設萬國電報公司於上海，增滬至香港各口海線。
units.en: Soon afterward, the British, French, German, and American ministers proposed founding an international telegraph company in Shanghai and laying additional submarine cables from Shanghai to Hong Kong and other ports.
units.literal: Before long, the ministers of Britain, France, Germany, and the United States proposed establishing an international telegraph company in Shanghai and adding submarine cables from Shanghai to the various ports of Hong Kong.

units.zh: 英使格維納並援案請增上海至寧波、溫州、福州、廈門、汕頭海線。
units.en: The British minister Grosvenor also invoked precedent to request submarine cables from Shanghai to Ningbo, Wenzhou, Fuzhou, Xiamen, and Shantou.
units.literal: The British minister Grosvenor also cited precedent in requesting additional submarine cables from Shanghai to Ningbo, Wenzhou, Fuzhou, Xiamen, and Shantou.

units.zh: 鴻章言：「宜令華商速設沿海陸線，以爭先著，使彼無利可圖，庶幾中止。
units.en: Li Hongzhang argued: "Chinese merchants should be urged to build coastal land lines quickly, seizing the initiative and leaving foreigners no profit to pursue—perhaps then they would abandon the plan.
units.literal: Li Hongzhang said: "Chinese merchants should be ordered to quickly install coastal land lines to seize the initiative, leaving them no profit to be gained, so that they might desist.

units.zh: 且從此海疆各省與京、外脈絡貫注，實與洋務海防有裨。
units.en: Moreover, coastal provinces would then be linked in continuous communication with the capital and abroad—a genuine benefit to foreign affairs and coastal defense.
units.literal: Moreover, from this the coastal provinces would be linked in continuous communication with the capital and foreign countries, which would truly benefit foreign affairs and coastal defense.

units.zh: 即商民轉輸貿易，消息靈通，為利更大。」
units.en: Merchants engaged in trade would benefit even more from rapid access to market intelligence."
units.literal: Even for merchants transporting goods and conducting trade, swift communication of news would bring even greater benefit."

units.zh: 從之。
units.en: The court agreed.
units.literal: The proposal was accepted.

units.zh: 而蘇州至浙、閩、粵陸線因之告成。
units.en: Land lines from Suzhou to Zhejiang, Fujian, and Guangdong were completed as a result.
units.literal: Accordingly, the land lines from Suzhou to Zhejiang, Fujian, and Guangdong were completed.

units.zh: 其時香港英商方欲設水線至廣州，粵督曾國荃亟造陸線以遏之。
units.en: British merchants in Hong Kong were then preparing to lay a submarine cable to Guangzhou. Zeng Guoquan, Governor-General of Guangdong, hastily built a land line to forestall them.
units.literal: At that time British merchants in Hong Kong were about to install a submarine cable to Guangzhou. The Governor-General of Guangdong Zeng Guoquan urgently built a land line to check them.

units.zh: 於是港線不得侵入粵境，英線不獲造至福州。
units.en: The Hong Kong cable was barred from entering Guangdong, and the British line was denied extension to Fuzhou.
units.literal: Thus the Hong Kong cable could not encroach into Guangdong territory, and the British line was not permitted to extend to Fuzhou.

units.zh: 而上海丹線、九龍英線先後毀去，或貲購之。
units.en: The Danish line in Shanghai and the British line in Kowloon were subsequently dismantled or bought out.
units.literal: Meanwhile the Danish line in Shanghai and the British line in Kowloon were successively destroyed or purchased.

units.zh: 沿海電線，其權悉操於中國之手。
units.en: Control over coastal telegraph lines passed entirely into Chinese hands.
units.literal: Control over coastal telegraph lines was entirely in China's hands.

units.zh: 此因外線之侵入而次第創設者也。
units.en: These lines were built in stages in response to foreign encroachment.
units.literal: These were established in sequence in response to the encroachment of foreign lines.

units.zh: 當沿海陸線未設之先，海疆萬里，消息阻絕，緩急無以為備。
units.en: Before coastal land lines existed, the ten-thousand-li maritime frontier was cut off from timely news, leaving no way to respond to emergencies.
units.literal: Before coastal land lines were installed, the maritime frontier stretched ten thousand li with communications cut off, leaving no means of preparation for emergencies.

units.zh: 御史陳啟泰上防海六策，其一言：「洋面既派兵輪分駐，即不可不設電線以通消息。
units.en: Censor Chen Qitai submitted six proposals for coastal defense, one of which argued: "Since gunboats are already stationed at sea, telegraph lines must be installed to relay intelligence.
units.literal: The censor Chen Qitai submitted six strategies for coastal defense, one of which stated: "Since gunboats have already been stationed on the open sea, telegraph lines must be installed to transmit news.

units.zh: 議者必以不急之務虛糜鉅款為疑。
units.en: Critics will surely object that this is a non-urgent expense that would squander large sums.
units.literal: Critics will surely doubt this as a non-urgent matter that would wastefully consume large funds.

units.zh: 不知非常之原，斷非省嗇所能集事。
units.en: They fail to see that extraordinary undertakings cannot be accomplished through penny-pinching alone.
units.literal: They do not understand that extraordinary undertakings cannot be accomplished through mere thrift.

units.zh: 即以目前而論，越南情形，每藉各國新聞紙以為耳目。
units.en: Even now, regarding Vietnam, we depend on foreign newspapers for our intelligence.
units.literal: Even at present, regarding conditions in Vietnam, we rely on foreign newspapers as our eyes and ears.

units.zh: 今年朝鮮之變，非由日本發來電信，中國尚不得知。
units.en: This year's crisis in Korea: had Japan not sent a telegram, China would still have been in the dark.
units.literal: This year's disturbances in Korea—had Japan not sent a telegram, China would still not have known.

units.zh: 軍情緊急，日夕萬狀，郵傳迂緩，既恐有誤機宜，藉助外人，事體更多窒礙，自不如招雇洋匠自行安設之為愈。
units.en: Military situations shift by the hour. The relay post is too slow and risks missing critical moments; relying on foreigners creates further complications. It would be better to hire Western technicians and install our own lines.
units.literal: Military situations are urgent with conditions changing by the day. Relay post is slow and circuitous, which risks missing critical timing. Relying on foreigners creates even more obstacles. It would be better to hire Western technicians and install the lines ourselves.

units.zh: 中國電報，似宜推廣各省海口，凡兵船寄椗之處，一律開辦。
units.en: China's telegraph network should be extended to every provincial port, with offices wherever naval vessels are stationed.
units.literal: China's telegraph network should be extended to the harbors of every province, establishing offices wherever naval vessels are stationed.

units.zh: 廣東瓊州之線逕達越南，奉天旅順之線逕達朝鮮，總期脈絡聯貫，呼應靈通，遇有警報，瞬息可至。」
units.en: A line from Qiongzhou, Guangdong, should run directly to Vietnam; one from Lüshun, Fengtian, directly to Korea. The goal is a connected network with rapid mutual response, so that alarms can be relayed in moments."
units.literal: A line from Qiongzhou in Guangdong should run directly to Vietnam; a line from Lüshun in Fengtian should run directly to Korea. The aim is continuous linkage and swift mutual response, so that when alarms arise, news can arrive in an instant."

units.zh: 下所司議行。
units.en: The memorial was referred to the relevant offices for deliberation and implementation.
units.literal: The memorial was referred to the responsible offices for deliberation and implementation.

units.zh: 十年，法、越事起，海防急，設線北塘以訖山海關，遞及於營口、旅順。
units.en: In 1884, with the Franco-Vietnamese conflict erupting and coastal defense urgent, lines were laid from Beitang to Shanhaiguan and onward to Yingkou and Lüshun.
units.literal: In the tenth year, the Franco-Vietnamese conflict arose and coastal defense became urgent. Lines were installed from Beitang to Shanhaiguan, extending in succession to Yingkou and Lüshun.

units.zh: 江督左宗棠則設長江線以通武漢，粵督張樹聲則設廣西線以達龍州。
units.en: Zuo Zongtang, Governor-General of Liangjiang, built Yangtze lines to Wuhan; Zhang Shusheng, Governor-General of Guangdong, built Guangxi lines to Longzhou.
units.literal: The Governor-General of Jiangsu Zuo Zongtang installed Yangtze lines connecting to Wuhan, while the Governor-General of Guangdong Zhang Shusheng installed Guangxi lines reaching Longzhou.

units.zh: 二十一年，中日戰事亟，慮直東一線有阻，接設老河口至西安線。
units.en: In 1895, with the Sino-Japanese War urgent and the Zhili-Shandong line at risk of disruption, a connecting line from Laohekou to Xi'an was built.
units.literal: In the twenty-first year, with the Sino-Japanese war urgent, fearing obstruction of the Zhili-Shandong line, a connecting line from Laohekou to Xi'an was installed.

units.zh: 是役江蘇增上海至獅子林、金山衛、乍浦，清江至青口、板浦，揚州至通州、泰州，鎮江至圌山關、天都廟，崇明至吳淞等線，而奉天至仁川電線先成於十一年。
units.en: During that war Jiangsu added lines from Shanghai to Shizilin, Jinshanwei, and Zhapu; from Qingjiang to Qingkou and Banpu; from Yangzhou to Tongzhou and Taizhou; from Zhenjiang to Tuanshan Pass and Tiandu Temple; and from Chongming to Wusong. The Fengtian-Incheon line had been completed earlier, in 1885.
units.literal: During that campaign Jiangsu added lines from Shanghai to Shizilin, Jinshanwei, and Zhapu; from Qingjiang to Qingkou and Banpu; from Yangzhou to Tongzhou and Taizhou; from Zhenjiang to Tuanshan Pass and Tiandu Temple; and from Chongming to Wusong. The Fengtian-Incheon telegraph line had been completed earlier in the eleventh year.

units.zh: 台灣以瀕海要區，十四年亦水陸線並設焉。
units.en: Taiwan, a critical coastal region, had both submarine and land lines installed in 1888.
units.literal: Taiwan, as a critical coastal region, also had both submarine and land lines installed in the fourteenth year.

units.zh: 此因海防緊要而次第安設者也。
units.en: These lines were built in stages in response to urgent coastal defense needs.
units.literal: These were installed in sequence because coastal defense was urgent.

units.zh: 滇、桂密邇越南、緬甸，邊備為急。
units.en: Yunnan and Guangxi lie adjacent to Vietnam and Burma, making frontier defense a pressing concern.
units.literal: Yunnan and Guangxi border Vietnam and Burma closely, making frontier defense urgent.

units.zh: 滇省電線，其始僅通鄂通蜀，與南寧接線之議，光緒十一年得請而未果行。
units.en: Yunnan's telegraph lines initially connected only to Hubei and Sichuan. A proposal to link with Nanning was approved in 1885 but never implemented.
units.literal: Yunnan's telegraph lines at first connected only to Hubei and Sichuan. A proposal to link with Nanning was approved in the eleventh year of Guangxu but was not carried out.

units.zh: 十三年，滇督岑毓英復言：「由緬入滇，以騰越為入境門戶，猶蒙自之于越南也。
units.en: In 1887, Cen Yuying, Governor-General of Yunnan, argued again: "Entry from Burma into Yunnan passes through Tengyue, just as entry from Vietnam passes through Mengzi.
units.literal: In the thirteenth year, the Governor-General of Yunnan Cen Yuying again stated: "Entry from Burma into Yunnan takes Tengyue as the gateway, just as Mengzi serves for Vietnam.

units.zh: 今英國有開辦通商之請，自當先事籌維。
units.en: Britain has now requested to open trade routes—we must prepare in advance.
units.literal: Now that Britain has requested to open trade, preparations should naturally be made in advance.

units.zh: 擬就粵西工匠到滇之便，即將省城至騰越一路安設電線，以通英緬聲息。」
units.en: While Guangxi artisans are available in Yunnan, we propose installing telegraph lines from the provincial capital to Tengyue to monitor developments in British Burma."
units.literal: Taking advantage of Guangxi artisans coming to Yunnan, telegraph lines are proposed along the route from the provincial capital to Tengyue to transmit news from Britain and Burma."

units.zh: 時粵督張之洞亦言：「廣西南界接壤滇邊，桂、滇皆西鄰越南，滇則西接緬甸。
units.en: Zhang Zhidong, Governor-General of Guangdong, also argued: "Guangxi's southern border adjoins Yunnan. Both provinces border Vietnam to the west; Yunnan also adjoins Burma.
units.literal: At the time the Governor-General of Guangdong Zhang Zhidong also stated: "Guangxi's southern border adjoins Yunnan's frontier. Both Guangxi and Yunnan border Vietnam to the west, while Yunnan also adjoins Burma on the west.

units.zh: 若僅恃由鄂入滇一線傳達電音，設有雷雨折斷電杆，阻滯堪虞。
units.en: If we rely solely on the single line from Hubei into Yunnan, a thunderstorm could snap the poles and cut communications—a serious risk.
units.literal: If one relies solely on the single line from Hubei into Yunnan to transmit telegrams, should thunderstorms break the poles, obstruction would be a serious concern.

units.zh: 且遇有軍務之時，由滇、川、滬、鄂展轉至粵，恐有交會壅滯之患。
units.en: In wartime, messages relayed from Yunnan, Sichuan, Shanghai, and Hubei through to Guangdong risk congestion at junction points.
units.literal: Moreover, in times of military operations, messages relayed from Yunnan, Sichuan, Shanghai, and Hubei to Guangdong would risk congestion at junction points.

units.zh: 已商之滇督，自剝隘至蒙自，由粵接造，並增騰越之線。」
units.en: I have consulted the Yunnan governor-general: Guangdong will build the connecting line from Bao'ai to Mengzi and add the Tengyue line as well."
units.literal: This has been discussed with the Governor-General of Yunnan: from Bao'ai to Mengzi, Guangdong will connect and build the line, and the Tengyue line will also be added."

units.zh: 疏入，報聞。
units.en: The memorial was submitted and acknowledged.
units.literal: The memorial was submitted and acknowledged.

units.zh: 蓋剝蒙設線，所以備越南；
units.en: The Bao'ai-Mengzi line was built to monitor Vietnam;
units.literal: The Bao'ai-Mengzi line was installed to guard against Vietnam;

units.zh: 騰越設線，所以備緬甸也。
units.en: the Tengyue line was built to monitor Burma.
units.literal: the Tengyue line was installed to guard against Burma.

units.zh: 吉林、黑龍江偪處俄疆，邊防尤要。
units.en: Jilin and Heilongjiang border Russian territory, making frontier defense especially critical.
units.literal: Jilin and Heilongjiang press against Russian territory, making frontier defense especially important.

units.zh: 十五年，自吉林省城設線至松花江南岸，歷茂興站、齊齊哈爾、布特哈、墨爾根、興安嶺、黑龍江以達黑河鎮，從練兵大臣穆圖善之言也。
units.en: In 1889, following Mutushan's proposal, a line was built from Jilin city to the south bank of the Songhua River, passing through Maoxing Station, Qiqihar, Buteha, Mo'ergen, Xing'an Ridge, and Heilongjiang to Heihe Town.
units.literal: In the fifteenth year, a line was installed from Jilin provincial capital to the south bank of the Songhua River, passing through Maoxing Station, Qiqihar, Buteha, Mo'ergen, Xing'an Ridge, and Heilongjiang to reach Heihe Town, following the proposal of the military training commissioner Mutushan.

units.zh: 十八年，陝甘總督楊昌濬言：「新疆西北鄰俄，西南與英屬部接壤，文報濡滯，貽誤必多。
units.en: In 1892, Yang Changjun, Governor-General of Shaanxi-Gansu, argued: "Xinjiang borders Russia to the northwest and British territories to the southwest. Delayed dispatches will surely cause serious errors.
units.literal: In the eighteenth year, Yang Changjun, Governor-General of Shaanxi-Gansu, stated: "Xinjiang borders Russia to the northwest and adjoins British territories to the southwest. Delayed official dispatches will surely cause many errors.

units.zh: 宜由肅州設線至新疆省城，及於伊犁、喀什噶爾。」
units.en: Lines should be built from Suzhou to the Xinjiang capital, and onward to Ili and Kashgar."
units.literal: Lines should be installed from Suzhou to the Xinjiang provincial capital, and onward to Ili and Kashgar."

units.zh: 宣統元年，桂撫張鳴岐疏陳設柳邕電線二千三百餘里。
units.en: In 1909, Zhang Mingqi, Governor of Guangxi, memorialized proposing a Liuzhou-Nanning telegraph line of over twenty-three hundred li.
units.literal: In the first year of Xuantong, the Governor of Guangxi Zhang Mingqi memorialized proposing the installation of the Liuzhou-Nanning telegraph line of more than twenty-three hundred li.

units.zh: 俱得請。
units.en: All were approved.
units.literal: All were approved.

units.zh: 此因邊備而增設者也。
units.en: These lines were added for frontier defense.
units.literal: These were added because of frontier defense needs.

units.zh: 初，奏設南北洋陸線，北端僅至天津。
units.en: When the north-south coastal land lines were first proposed, the northern terminus reached only Tianjin.
units.literal: At first, when the Northern and Southern Seas land lines were proposed, the northern terminus reached only Tianjin.

units.zh: 法事將起，出使大臣曾紀澤請接營近畿電線，謂可壯聲威以保和局，靈呼應以利戰事。
units.en: As the French crisis loomed, Envoy Zeng Jize requested extending telegraph lines into the capital region, arguing this would bolster prestige to preserve peace and enable rapid coordination in wartime.
units.literal: As the French affair was about to arise, the envoy Zeng Jizi requested connecting telegraph lines near the capital, saying this could bolster prestige to preserve peace and enable swift coordination to benefit military operations.

units.zh: 事下所司，與鴻章議展拓之法。
units.en: The matter was referred to the relevant offices to discuss extension plans with Li Hongzhang.
units.literal: The matter was referred to the responsible offices to discuss methods of extension with Li Hongzhang.

units.zh: 鴻章言：「神京為中外所歸鄉，發號施令，需用倍切。
units.en: Li Hongzhang replied: "The capital is the center to which all look. Issuing commands from there demands the utmost urgency.
units.literal: Li Hongzhang stated: "The divine capital is where Chinese and foreign alike look for direction. Issuing commands requires redoubled urgency.

units.zh: 前於創辦電報之初，頗慮士大夫見聞未熟，或滋口舌，是以暫從天津設起，漸開風氣。
units.en: When telegraphy was first introduced, I feared that unfamiliar scholar-officials might raise objections. We therefore started from Tianjin to gradually acclimate public opinion.
units.literal: When telegraphy was first established, there was considerable concern that scholar-officials, unfamiliar with it, might raise objections. Therefore it was temporarily started from Tianjin to gradually open minds.

units.zh: 其于軍國要務，裨益實多。
units.en: Its benefits for military and state affairs have been considerable.
units.literal: Its benefits for military and state affairs have been considerable.

units.zh: 今總理衙門與曾紀澤皆以近畿展線為善策，擬暫設至通州，逐漸接展至京。」
units.en: Both the Zongli Yamen and Zeng Jize now agree that extending lines into the capital region is sound policy. We propose building first to Tongzhou, then gradually extending to Beijing."
units.literal: Now both the Zongli Yamen and Zeng Jizi regard extending lines into the capital region as a sound policy. It is proposed to install temporarily to Tongzhou and gradually extend to the capital."

units.zh: 允行。
units.en: This was approved.
units.literal: This was approved.

units.zh: 逾年，津線遂逾通州達京師。
units.en: A year later the Tianjin line passed through Tongzhou and reached the capital.
units.literal: More than a year later, the Tianjin line passed Tongzhou and reached the capital.

units.zh: 自時厥後，各省咸知電報之利。
units.en: From that point on, every province recognized the value of telegraphy.
units.literal: From that time onward, every province came to know the benefits of telegraphy.

units.zh: 或本無而創設，或已有而引伸。
units.en: Some provinces built lines where none existed; others extended existing networks.
units.literal: Some established it where none had existed; others extended lines already in place.

units.zh: 其尤要之區，則陸線、水線兼營，正線、支線並設，縱橫全國，經緯相維。
units.en: In the most critical regions, land and submarine lines were built together, main and branch lines side by side, forming a nationwide crisscross network.
units.literal: In the most critical regions, land lines and submarine cables were operated together, main lines and branch lines installed side by side, spanning the entire country in a crisscross network of warp and weft.

units.zh: 直、蘇、粵、桂、滇、魯、鄂諸省，設局多至二十餘所，餘省亦十餘局或數局有差。
units.en: Zhili, Jiangsu, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Shandong, and Hubei each had as many as twenty offices or more; other provinces had ten or more, or a varying number.
units.literal: In Zhili, Jiangsu, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Shandong, and Hubei, as many as twenty or more offices were established. Other provinces had ten or more offices, or a varying number of several offices.

units.zh: 其互相銜接者，京師之線所達，曰庫倫、濟南、太原。
units.en: Lines from the capital connected to Urga, Jinan, and Taiyuan.
units.literal: Among those interconnected, the lines from the capital reached Urga, Jinan, and Taiyuan.

units.zh: 天津之線所達，曰奉天。
units.en: Lines from Tianjin reached Fengtian.
units.literal: The lines from Tianjin reached Fengtian.

units.zh: 奉天之線所達，曰天津、旅順、吉林。
units.en: Lines from Fengtian reached Tianjin, Lüshun, and Jilin.
units.literal: The lines from Fengtian reached Tianjin, Lüshun, and Jilin.

units.zh: 吉林之線所達，曰海參崴、齊齊哈爾、奉天。
units.en: Lines from Jilin reached Vladivostok, Qiqihar, and Fengtian.
units.literal: The lines from Jilin reached Vladivostok, Qiqihar, and Fengtian.

units.zh: 黑龍江之線所達，曰吉林、海蘭泡。
units.en: Lines from Heilongjiang reached Jilin and Blagoveshchensk.
units.literal: The lines from Heilongjiang reached Jilin and Blagoveshchensk.

units.zh: 江蘇之線所達，曰京師、蕪湖。
units.en: Lines from Jiangsu reached the capital and Wuhu.
units.literal: The lines from Jiangsu reached the capital and Wuhu.

units.zh: 安徽之線所達，曰江寧、九江。
units.en: Lines from Anhui reached Jiangning and Jiujiang.
units.literal: The lines from Anhui reached Jiangning and Jiujiang.

units.zh: 山西之線所達，曰京師、西安。
units.en: Lines from Shanxi reached the capital and Xi'an.
units.literal: The lines from Shanxi reached the capital and Xi'an.

units.zh: 山東之線所達，曰京師、開封、清江浦。
units.en: Lines from Shandong reached the capital, Kaifeng, and Qingjiangpu.
units.literal: The lines from Shandong reached the capital, Kaifeng, and Qingjiangpu.

units.zh: 河南之線所達，曰京師、濟南、西安。
units.en: Lines from Henan reached the capital, Jinan, and Xi'an.
units.literal: The lines from Henan reached the capital, Jinan, and Xi'an.

units.zh: 陝西之線所達，曰開封、太原、蘭州、漢口。
units.en: Lines from Shaanxi reached Kaifeng, Taiyuan, Lanzhou, and Hankou.
units.literal: The lines from Shaanxi reached Kaifeng, Taiyuan, Lanzhou, and Hankou.

units.zh: 甘肅之線所達，曰迪化、西安。
units.en: Lines from Gansu reached Dihua and Xi'an.
units.literal: The lines from Gansu reached Dihua and Xi'an.

units.zh: 新疆之線所達，曰蘭州。
units.en: Lines from Xinjiang reached Lanzhou.
units.literal: The lines from Xinjiang reached Lanzhou.

units.zh: 浙江之線所達，曰上海、福州。
units.en: Lines from Zhejiang reached Shanghai and Fuzhou.
units.literal: The lines from Zhejiang reached Shanghai and Fuzhou.

units.zh: 江西之線所達，曰廣州、蕪湖、河口。
units.en: Lines from Jiangxi reached Guangzhou, Wuhu, and Hekou.
units.literal: The lines from Jiangxi reached Guangzhou, Wuhu, and Hekou.

units.zh: 湖北之線所達，曰九江、成都、長沙、鄭州。
units.en: Lines from Hubei reached Jiujiang, Chengdu, Changsha, and Zhengzhou.
units.literal: The lines from Hubei reached Jiujiang, Chengdu, Changsha, and Zhengzhou.

units.zh: 湖南之線所達，曰漢口、桂林。
units.en: Lines from Hunan reached Hankou and Guilin.
units.literal: The lines from Hunan reached Hankou and Guilin.

units.zh: 四川之線所達，曰漢口。
units.en: Lines from Sichuan reached Hankou.
units.literal: The lines from Sichuan reached Hankou.

units.zh: 福建之線所達，曰杭州、廣州。
units.en: Lines from Fujian reached Hangzhou and Guangzhou.
units.literal: The lines from Fujian reached Hangzhou and Guangzhou.

units.zh: 廣東之線所達，曰福州、梧州、九江。
units.en: Lines from Guangdong reached Fuzhou, Wuzhou, and Jiujiang.
units.literal: The lines from Guangdong reached Fuzhou, Wuzhou, and Jiujiang.

units.zh: 廣西之線所達，曰長沙、廣州。
units.en: Lines from Guangxi reached Changsha and Guangzhou.
units.literal: The lines from Guangxi reached Changsha and Guangzhou.

units.zh: 雲南之線所達，曰漢口、重慶、八莫、南寧。
units.en: Lines from Yunnan reached Hankou, Chongqing, Bhamo, and Nanning.
units.literal: The lines from Yunnan reached Hankou, Chongqing, Bhamo, and Nanning.

units.zh: 貴州之線所達，曰重慶。
units.en: Lines from Guizhou reached Chongqing.
units.literal: The lines from Guizhou reached Chongqing.

units.zh: 外蒙則達京師、張家口焉。
units.en: Outer Mongolia was linked to the capital and Zhangjiakou.
units.literal: Outer Mongolia reached the capital and Zhangjiakou.

units.zh: 瀕海之區則設海線。
units.en: Coastal regions were served by submarine cables.
units.literal: In coastal regions submarine cables were installed.

units.zh: 直隸自大沽以通之罘。
units.en: In Zhili, Dagu was linked to Yantai.
units.literal: From Zhili, Dagu connected to Yantai.

units.zh: 江蘇自上海東通長崎，北通之罘、大沽，南通廈門、香港。
units.en: From Shanghai in Jiangsu, cables ran east to Nagasaki, north to Yantai and Dagu, and south to Xiamen and Hong Kong.
units.literal: From Jiangsu, Shanghai connected east to Nagasaki, north to Yantai and Dagu, and south to Xiamen and Hong Kong.

units.zh: 廣東自香港通海防、新嘉坡、廈門、上海、馬尼喇。
units.en: From Hong Kong in Guangdong, cables ran to Haiphong, Singapore, Xiamen, Shanghai, and Manila.
units.literal: From Guangdong, Hong Kong connected to Haiphong, Singapore, Xiamen, Shanghai, and Manila.

units.zh: 山東自之罘通大沽、旅順、威海衛、青島、上海。
units.en: From Yantai in Shandong, cables ran to Dagu, Lüshun, Weihaiwei, Qingdao, and Shanghai.
units.literal: From Shandong, Yantai connected to Dagu, Lüshun, Weihaiwei, Qingdao, and Shanghai.

units.zh: 福建自川石山通台灣淡水，自廈門通上海、香港。
units.en: From Fujian, Chuanshi Mountain was linked to Tamsui in Taiwan, and Xiamen to Shanghai and Hong Kong.
units.literal: From Fujian, Chuanshi Mountain connected to Tamsui in Taiwan, and Xiamen connected to Shanghai and Hong Kong.

units.zh: 蓋總計陸線之設，不下四萬里有奇，而水線不與焉。
units.en: Land lines totaled over forty thousand li—not counting submarine cables.
units.literal: In all, land lines installed amounted to no less than forty thousand odd li, not counting submarine cables.

units.zh: 電報設局，亦如輪船招商之例，商力舉辦而官董其成，謂官督商辦也。
units.en: Telegraph offices were established on the China Merchants model: merchants provided capital while officials supervised operations—the government-supervised, merchant-operated system.
units.literal: Telegraph offices were established following the China Merchants Steam Navigation model: merchant capital undertook the work while officials supervised its completion. This was called government-supervised, merchant-operated.

units.zh: 津滬一線，其始倡以官帑，未幾即歸商局，醵貲至二百餘萬。
units.en: The Tianjin-Shanghai line was initially funded by the government, but soon passed to the merchant bureau, which raised over two million taels in capital.
units.literal: The Tianjin-Shanghai line was initially proposed with official funds, but before long it passed to the merchant bureau, which raised capital exceeding two million.

units.zh: 而各省電線不盡由商辦者，良以商人重利，入貲則權子母、計盈虧，其于海防邊備情勢緩急，國內交通利便與否，不以措意。
units.en: Not all provincial lines were merchant-operated, because merchants prioritize profit—investing capital to calculate returns, with little regard for coastal and frontier defense or the convenience of domestic communications.
units.literal: Not all provincial telegraph lines were merchant-operated, because merchants value profit. When investing capital they calculate principal and interest and weigh gains and losses. They pay no heed to the urgency of coastal and frontier defense, or whether domestic communications are convenient.

units.zh: 往往一線，官辦商辦，參互錯綜，大率以官辦補商辦之不足。
units.en: A single line often combined government and merchant operation in complex ways, with government operation generally filling gaps left by merchant operation.
units.literal: Often a single line would mix government and merchant operation in complex combination, generally with government operation supplementing merchant operation's inadequacies.

units.zh: 兩粵電線，廣州至龍州則屬之官，至梧州則屬之商。
units.en: In the two Guang provinces, the Guangzhou-Longzhou line was government-operated, while the line to Wuzhou was merchant-operated.
units.literal: Among the telegraph lines of the two Guang provinces, the line from Guangzhou to Longzhou belonged to the government, while that to Wuzhou belonged to merchants.

units.zh: 欽、廉、雷、瓊及鎮南關、虎門，則官商協力。
units.en: Qinzhou, Lianzhou, Leizhou, Qiongzhou, Zhennan Pass, and Humen were built through joint government-merchant effort.
units.literal: Qinzhou, Lianzhou, Leizhou, Qiongzhou, Zhennan Pass, and Humen were joint government-merchant efforts.

units.zh: 而滇線一自鄂入，一自蜀入，一自桂入。
units.en: Yunnan's lines entered from Hubei, Sichuan, and Guangxi.
units.literal: Yunnan's lines entered from Hubei, from Sichuan, and from Guangxi.

units.zh: 西安迄嘉峪關、甘、新、奉、吉、黑等省，通州至承德，陸線俱官為之。
units.en: Land lines from Xi'an to Jiayuguan and in Gansu, Xinjiang, Fengtian, Jilin, Heilongjiang, and other provinces, as well as from Tongzhou to Chengde, were all government-built.
units.literal: Land lines from Xi'an to Jiayuguan, and in Gansu, Xinjiang, Fengtian, Jilin, Heilongjiang, and other provinces, as well as from Tongzhou to Chengde, were all built by the government.

units.zh: 此類是也。
units.en: These fell into that category.
units.literal: These were of that type.

units.zh: 然由滬達粵之線，本為防止外線而設，需費四十餘萬兩，咸由商力措備。
units.en: The Shanghai-Guangdong line, however, was originally built to forestall foreign encroachment. It cost over four hundred thousand taels, all raised by merchants.
units.literal: However, the line from Shanghai to Guangdong was originally established to prevent foreign lines from encroaching. It required over four hundred thousand taels, all raised by merchant capital.

units.zh: 其時香港英人並欲引線達廣州，亦賴華合公司預設線至九龍，其謀始戢。
units.en: British interests in Hong Kong then sought to extend a line to Guangzhou, but the Chinese Merchants' Union Company's preemptive line to Kowloon forced them to abandon the plan.
units.literal: At that time the British in Hong Kong also wished to extend a line to Guangzhou. It was only because the Chinese Merchants' Union Company preemptively installed a line to Kowloon that their scheme was finally abandoned.

units.zh: 方華合公司設線九龍也，華民抗拒，英商撓阻，其勢洶洶。
units.en: When the Chinese Merchants' Union Company built its Kowloon line, Chinese residents resisted and British merchants obstructed—the confrontation was fierce.
units.literal: When the Chinese Merchants' Union Company was installing its line to Kowloon, Chinese residents resisted and British merchants obstructed—the situation was tumultuous.

units.zh: 公司商人何獻墀等排眾難而為之，不為所屈，卒底於成。
units.en: Company merchants including He Xianci pressed ahead despite fierce opposition, refusing to yield, and ultimately completed the project.
units.literal: Company merchants such as He Xianci overcame the crowd's difficulties to carry it out, refusing to be deterred, and ultimately brought it to completion.

units.zh: 中日戰事棘，引襄陽線千餘里直達西安，俾京、滬軍報不至梗阻。
units.en: During the Sino-Japanese War, a line of over a thousand li from Xiangyang directly to Xi'an was built to keep military dispatches between Beijing and Shanghai from being cut off.
units.literal: When the Sino-Japanese war became urgent, a line of over a thousand li from Xiangyang directly to Xi'an was installed so that military dispatches between the capital and Shanghai would not be obstructed.

units.zh: 而張家口至恰克圖一線，以俄使援約相促，亦由商局集金六十餘萬兩，接線二千七百餘里，經營至二三年之久，工鉅費繁，為全國最。
units.en: The Zhangjiakou-Kyakhta line, pressed by the Russian envoy under treaty obligations, was also funded by the merchant bureau with over six hundred thousand taels, spanning over twenty-seven hundred li. Two or three years in the making, it was the largest and costliest project in the country.
units.literal: The Zhangjiakou-Kyakhta line, urged on by the Russian envoy citing treaty obligations, was also funded by the merchant bureau with over six hundred thousand taels, connecting lines of over twenty-seven hundred li. It took two or three years to complete—the largest and costliest project in the country.

units.zh: 此外造成之線，不能里數，其所裨殆非淺鮮矣。
units.en: Countless other lines were built as well—their contributions were considerable.
units.literal: Beyond this, completed lines cannot be counted in li—their benefits were surely not slight.

units.zh: 二十五年，大學士徐桐言電報局獲利不貲，並無裨益公家之實。
units.en: In 1899, Grand Secretary Xu Tong argued that the telegraph bureau reaped enormous profits while bringing no real benefit to the state.
units.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, Grand Secretary Xu Tong stated that the telegraph bureau reaped immeasurable profit yet brought no real benefit to the state.

units.zh: 廷臣亦有以招商、電報各局假公濟私為言者。
units.en: Court officials also charged that the China Merchants and telegraph bureaus used public office for private gain.
units.literal: Court officials also spoke of the China Merchants and telegraph bureaus using public office for private gain.

units.zh: 俱下協辦大學士剛毅查復。
units.en: All were referred to Associate Grand Secretary Gangyi for investigation.
units.literal: All were referred to Associate Grand Secretary Gangyi for investigation and reply.

units.zh: 剛毅時以事銜命赴蘇，尋疏陳：「電局自恰線成後，所虧至鉅，俟有贏餘，歲輸南北洋學款十二萬四千兩。」
units.en: Gangyi was then on assignment in Suzhou. He soon reported: "Since the Kyakhta line was completed, the telegraph bureau's losses have been enormous. When surpluses arise, it remits 124,000 taels annually for Northern and Southern Seas educational funds."
units.literal: Gangyi was then on assignment in Suzhou on imperial orders. He soon memorialized: "Since the Kyakhta line was completed, the telegraph bureau's losses have been enormous. When there are surpluses, it remits one hundred twenty-four thousand taels annually for Northern and Southern Seas educational funds."

units.zh: 報可。
units.en: The report was approved.
units.literal: The report was approved.

units.zh: 明年，廷臣復言電局利權太重，宜遴員接辦。
units.en: The following year, court officials again argued that the telegraph bureau wielded too much profit and authority, and that suitable officials should be appointed to take over.
units.literal: The following year, court officials again stated that the telegraph bureau's profit and authority were too great, and that suitable officials should be selected to take over.

units.zh: 詔飭宣懷按年冊報收支款目，官電應免收費。
units.en: An edict ordered Sheng Xuanhuai to submit annual accounts of income and expenditures, and mandated that official telegrams be sent free of charge.
units.literal: An edict ordered Sheng Xuanhuai to report income and expenditures annually in registers, and that official telegrams should be sent free of charge.

units.zh: 宣懷上疏，略言：「電局本系集華商合眾之力，以與洋商爭衡，旁觀每驚為大利所叢，其實析分千百股商，仍皆寸寸銖銖之微利。
units.en: Sheng Xuanhuai submitted a memorial arguing: "The telegraph bureau was founded to pool Chinese merchant capital against foreign competition. Outsiders marvel at its profits, but divided among thousands of shareholders, each earns only modest returns.
units.literal: Sheng Xuanhuai submitted a memorial stating in summary: "The telegraph bureau originally gathered the combined strength of Chinese merchants to compete with foreign merchants. Observers often marvel at it as a concentration of great profit, but in fact, divided among thousands of shareholders, each receives only tiny incremental gains.

units.zh: 近年電線開拓日廣，則局用及修線養線之費亦日增。
units.en: As telegraph lines have expanded in recent years, bureau expenses and line maintenance costs have risen accordingly.
units.literal: In recent years, as telegraph lines have expanded daily, bureau expenses and costs for maintaining and repairing lines have also increased daily.

units.zh: 上年因中俄條約，接造恰克圖之線用費六十餘萬兩，未請官款，悉系電商集貲辦成。
units.en: Last year, under the Sino-Russian treaty, the Kyakhta connecting line cost over six hundred thousand taels—all raised by telegraph merchants, with no government funds requested.
units.literal: Last year, pursuant to the Sino-Russian treaty, the Kyakhta connecting line cost over six hundred thousand taels. No official funds were requested—all was raised and completed by telegraph merchants.

units.zh: 沙漠荒僻之區，絕少報費，而常年用數尤鉅。
units.en: Desert and remote regions generate almost no telegram revenue, yet operating costs remain enormous.
units.literal: In desert and remote regions, telegram fees are extremely scarce, yet annual operating expenses are especially heavy.

units.zh: 至本年應辦之工，因辦理鐵路，盧溝橋至保定線已造成，又須造保定至漢口幹線。
units.en: This year's projects include the completed Lugou Bridge-Baoding line for railway construction, and the Baoding-Hankou trunk line still to be built.
units.literal: As for this year's required work: because of railway construction, the Lugou Bridge-Baoding line has been completed, and the Baoding-Hankou trunk line must also be built.

units.zh: 因辦理海防，乃須造寧波至溫州之線。
units.en: For coastal defense, the Ningbo-Wenzhou line must be built.
units.literal: Because of coastal defense, the Ningbo-Wenzhou line must be built.

units.zh: 總理衙門因洋人之請，則須造山東泰安、沂州之線。
units.en: At foreign request through the Zongli Yamen, lines to Taian and Yizhou in Shandong must be built.
units.literal: At the Zongli Yamen's request on behalf of foreigners, the Shandong Taian and Yizhou lines must be built.

units.zh: 此外各路加線要工，絡繹不絕，官款並無可籌，皆借股商之力，以赴公家之急。
units.en: Branch lines and essential work continue without cease. With no government funds available, merchant shareholders bear the burden of meeting the state's urgent needs.
units.literal: Beyond this, branch lines and essential work on various routes continue without cease. No official funds can be raised—all rely on merchant shareholders' strength to meet the state's urgent needs.

units.zh: 總局收支各賬，均系按年刊布。
units.en: The head office publishes all income and expenditure accounts annually.
units.literal: All accounts of income and expenditure at the head office are published annually.

units.zh: 各局詳細坐簿，亦任股商隨時查閱。
units.en: Detailed ledgers at each office are open for shareholder inspection at any time.
units.literal: Detailed ledgers at each office are also open for shareholders to inspect at any time.

units.zh: 一出一入，眾見眾聞，非如官中所辦報銷，出於一二人之手者可比。
units.en: Every transaction is open to public scrutiny—unlike official reimbursements handled by one or two individuals.
units.literal: Every expenditure and receipt is seen and known by all—not comparable to official reimbursement handled by one or two persons.

units.zh: 原奏所疑各節，似屬不知此中原委。
units.en: The doubts raised in the original memorial seem to stem from ignorance of these facts.
units.literal: The various points doubted in the original memorial seem to stem from ignorance of these underlying facts.

units.zh: 至官報之費，前定章程，擬一半報效，一半給貲，期於官商兼顧，持久不廢，仍宜照舊辦理，以維大局。」
units.en: Regarding official telegram fees, the established regulations split costs evenly between tribute and payment to balance government and merchant interests for long-term sustainability. These arrangements should remain in place to preserve stability."
units.literal: As for official telegram fees, the previously established regulations proposed half as tribute and half as payment, aiming to balance government and merchant interests for lasting operation. These should still be handled as before to preserve the overall arrangement."

units.zh: 報聞。
units.en: The memorial was submitted and acknowledged.
units.literal: The memorial was submitted and acknowledged.

units.zh: 宣懷時綜司輪、電兩局，疊被指摘。
units.en: Sheng Xuanhuai, then overseeing both the steam navigation and telegraph bureaus, faced repeated criticism.
units.literal: Sheng Xuanhuai then supervised both the steam navigation and telegraph bureaus and was repeatedly criticized.

units.zh: 二十八年，言於直督袁世凱：「電報宜歸官有。
units.en: In 1902, he told Yuan Shikai, Governor-General of Zhili: "Telegraphy should be placed under government ownership.
units.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, he said to Yuan Shikai, Governor-General of Zhili: "Telegraphy should be placed under government ownership.

units.zh: 輪船純系商業，可易督辦，不可歸官。」
units.en: Steam navigation is purely commercial—it can change supervisors but should not be nationalized."
units.literal: Steam navigation is purely commercial—it can change supervisors but should not be placed under government ownership."

units.zh: 世凱謀諸執政者，以為然，聞於上。
units.en: Yuan Shikai consulted the ruling officials, who agreed, and reported to the throne.
units.literal: Yuan Shikai consulted the ruling officials, who agreed, and reported to the throne.

units.zh: 尋命世凱督辦電局，候補侍郎吳和喜副之。
units.en: Yuan Shikai was soon appointed to supervise the telegraph bureau, with Expectant Vice Minister Wu Hexi as his deputy.
units.literal: Soon Yuan Shikai was ordered to supervise the telegraph bureau, with Expectant Vice Minister Wu Hexi as his deputy.

units.zh: 明詔發還商股，不遽予行。
units.en: An explicit edict ordered the return of merchant shares, but this was not immediately carried out.
units.literal: An explicit edict ordered the return of merchant shares, but this was not immediately carried out.

units.zh: 眾商洶懼，爭欲持券售之外人。
units.en: Merchants panicked and rushed to sell their shares to foreigners.
units.literal: Merchants were alarmed and clamored to sell their shares to foreigners.

units.zh: 宣懷力遏之，乃已。
units.en: Sheng Xuanhuai forcefully stopped them, and the crisis passed.
units.literal: Sheng Xuanhuai forcefully stopped them, and the matter ceased.

units.zh: 尋詔原有商股一仍其舊，蓋其時僅易一商股官辦之局而已。
units.en: An edict soon restored the original merchant shares. At that point, only the bureau's designation changed from merchant to government operation.
units.literal: Soon an edict restored the original merchant shares as before. At that time, only the bureau's designation changed from merchant shares to government operation.

units.zh: 三十四年，郵傳設部已二年，將以全國電局為實行部轄之計。
units.en: In 1908, two years after the Ministry of Posts and Communications was established, plans were made to bring all telegraph bureaus nationwide under ministry jurisdiction.
units.literal: In the thirty-fourth year, two years after the Ministry of Posts and Communications was established, plans were made to bring all telegraph bureaus nationwide under the ministry's jurisdiction.

units.zh: 郵傳部尚書陳璧疏言：「電報為交通全國機關。
units.en: Minister Chen Bi of Posts and Communications memorialized: "The telegraph is the mechanism for connecting the entire country.
units.literal: Minister of Posts and Communications Chen Bi memorialized: "The telegraph is the mechanism for connecting the entire country.

units.zh: 各國電報之權皆操諸國家。
units.en: In every country, telegraph authority rests with the state.
units.literal: In every country, telegraph authority is held by the state.

units.zh: 中國電報，創始原歸商辦。
units.en: China's telegraph was originally merchant-operated.
units.literal: China's telegraph was originally established under merchant operation.

units.zh: 而光緒初年，商股微薄，仍賴官力以為補助，非完全商辦也。
units.en: But in the early Guangxu era, merchant capital was thin and relied on government support—it was never fully merchant-operated.
units.literal: But in the early Guangxu years, merchant shares were meager and still relied on government support as supplement—it was not fully merchant-operated.

units.zh: 歷年獲利，約計五六百萬。
units.en: Accumulated profits over the years totaled roughly five or six million taels.
units.literal: Profits accumulated over the years totaled approximately five or six million.

units.zh: 果使全國交通推行無阻，則富商即可富國，亦何必別議更張？
units.en: If nationwide communications functioned smoothly, wealthy merchants could enrich the nation—why change the system?
units.literal: If nationwide communications could be promoted without obstruction, then wealthy merchants could enrich the nation—why discuss changing the system?

units.zh: 乃觀商線所至之處，皆屬市鎮都會，而邊遠省分，如云、貴、廣西、甘肅、新疆，商人以無利可圖，均推歸官辦。
units.en: Yet merchant lines reach only market towns and major cities. In remote provinces—Yunnan, Guizhou, Guangxi, Gansu, Xinjiang—merchants, finding no profit, pushed responsibility back to the government.
units.literal: Yet observing where merchant lines reach, they are all market towns and major cities. In remote provinces such as Yunnan, Guizhou, Guangxi, Gansu, and Xinjiang, merchants, finding no profit, all pushed responsibility back to government operation.

units.zh: 雖商力實有未逮，而顧私利、忘遠略，實悖朝廷立部之初心。
units.en: Though merchant capacity was genuinely limited, prizing private profit over long-range strategy betrayed the court's purpose in establishing the ministry.
units.literal: Although merchant capacity was genuinely insufficient, prizing private profit and forgetting long-range strategy truly betrayed the court's original purpose in establishing the ministry.

units.zh: 衡以中國近狀，自非改為官辦，無以定區畫之方，即末由收擴充之效。
units.en: Given China's current condition, only government operation can establish a comprehensive plan and achieve meaningful expansion.
units.literal: Weighing China's recent condition, unless it is changed to government operation, there is no way to establish a comprehensive plan, nor to achieve expansion.

units.zh: 東西各國，電線如織，策應靈通，故伏莽方生，旋就撲滅。
units.en: In Western nations, telegraph lines crisscross the land with swift coordination, suppressing unrest almost as soon as it arises.
units.literal: In Eastern and Western countries, telegraph lines are woven like fabric, with swift mutual coordination, so that bandits barely arise before being suppressed.

units.zh: 中國電報，無論要荒，即腹地稍僻者，亦多缺而未舉。
units.en: China's telegraph network has gaps everywhere—from frontier wilderness to moderately remote interior regions.
units.literal: China's telegraph network, whether in frontier wilderness or even slightly remote interior regions, has many gaps where lines have not been established.

units.zh: 一旦有事，道途修阻，聲息不通，實于軍務有礙。
units.en: In an emergency, long distances and obstructed routes would cut communications—a serious handicap in military affairs.
units.literal: Once an emergency arises, roads are long and obstructed and communications cut off—this truly hampers military affairs.

units.zh: 況當百度維新，外交內政關係非輕，稍滯交通，輒形扞格。
units.en: At a time of comprehensive reform, foreign and domestic affairs depend heavily on communications—any delay creates friction.
units.literal: Moreover, at a time of comprehensive reform, foreign and domestic affairs are weighty matters. Any delay in communications immediately creates friction.

units.zh: 近來科布多、川、藏、蒙古、閩、浙、江西、蘇、松紛紛請設電線。
units.en: Recently Kobdo, Sichuan, Tibet, Mongolia, Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, and Songjiang have all petitioned for telegraph lines.
units.literal: Recently Kobdo, Sichuan, Tibet, Mongolia, Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, and Songjiang have all petitioned to install telegraph lines.

units.zh: 本年四月，奉旨迅設貴陽至義興電線。
units.en: In April of this year, an imperial edict ordered the rapid installation of the Guiyang-Yixing telegraph line.
units.literal: In the fourth month of this year, an imperial edict ordered the rapid installation of the Guiyang-Yixing telegraph line.

units.zh: 又陸軍部以秋間江、鄂各軍在安徽會操，請設安慶至太湖電線。
units.en: The Army Ministry also requested an Anqing-Taihu line for autumn joint exercises by Jiangsu and Hubei troops in Anhui.
units.literal: The Army Ministry also requested the Anqing-Taihu telegraph line for the autumn joint exercises of Jiangsu and Hubei troops in Anhui.

units.zh: 外務部請設川、藏通印度電線，以為收贖英人江孜線路張本。
units.en: The Foreign Ministry requested a Sichuan-Tibet-India line as groundwork for recovering the British line at Gyantse.
units.literal: The Foreign Ministry requested a Sichuan-Tibet-India telegraph line as groundwork for recovering the British line at Gyantse.

units.zh: 湖北官電局以賠累不堪，請改歸部辦。
units.en: The Hubei official telegraph bureau, unable to sustain its losses, requested transfer to ministry operation.
units.literal: The Hubei official telegraph bureau, unable to bear its losses, requested transfer to ministry operation.

units.zh: 紛來沓至，均為不可稍緩之圖。
units.en: Requests poured in—all projects that could not be delayed.
units.literal: Requests poured in one after another—all projects that could not be delayed even slightly.

units.zh: 核計各省請設各線，不下萬有餘里，工程當在一百餘萬以上。
units.en: Lines requested by the provinces total over ten thousand li, with engineering costs exceeding one million taels.
units.literal: Counting all lines requested by the provinces, they amount to no less than ten thousand odd li, with engineering costs exceeding one million.

units.zh: 且此萬餘里，半皆荒村僻壤，報務不多，增一線即賠一線之本，修一里即虧一里之費。
units.en: Moreover, half of these ten thousand li traverse remote villages and wasteland with little traffic. Each new line loses money; each li repaired adds to the deficit.
units.literal: Moreover, of these ten thousand odd li, half are remote villages and wasteland with little telegram traffic. Each new line loses on its principal; each li repaired loses on its cost.

units.zh: 前此添設雲、貴一二邊省電線，各股商尚慮虧損。
units.en: When lines were added in Yunnan, Guizhou, and other frontier provinces, shareholders already feared losses.
units.literal: Previously, when adding telegraph lines in Yunnan, Guizhou, and other frontier provinces, shareholders still feared losses.

units.zh: 今統籌荒瘠之區，更難著手。
units.en: Planning lines through barren, impoverished regions makes the task even harder.
units.literal: Now, planning for barren and impoverished regions, it is even harder to proceed.

units.zh: 至利則歸己，損則歸公，恐亦無此情理。
units.en: Profits to oneself while losses fall on the state—surely no one would accept such terms.
units.literal: As for profits going to oneself while losses go to the state—surely there is no such logic.

units.zh: 此展線之宜歸官辦者也。
units.en: This is why line expansion should fall under government operation.
units.literal: This is why line expansion should be placed under government operation.

units.zh: 各省線路，待修者眾，朽敗難支，而陝、豫、閩三省尤甚。
units.en: Many provincial lines await repair, decayed and barely functional—especially in Shaanxi, Henan, and Fujian.
units.literal: Among provincial lines, many await repair, decayed and barely holding together, especially in Shaanxi, Henan, and Fujian.

units.zh: 設遇軍興倉猝，何堪設想。
units.en: If war broke out suddenly, the consequences are unthinkable.
units.literal: If war should arise suddenly, the consequences are unthinkable.

units.zh: 現在遴員調查，通盤籌畫，尚有應移近鐵路者，有關係交涉亟須先佔者，有文報日多應行添線者。
units.en: Officials are now surveying and planning comprehensively: some lines should be relocated near railways; some involving diplomatic relations must be secured first; others need expansion as official dispatches increase.
units.literal: Officials are now being selected to investigate and plan comprehensively. Some lines should be relocated near railways; some involving diplomatic relations must be preemptively secured; some require additional lines as official dispatches increase daily.

units.zh: 次第修舉，工費浩繁，需銀約五六十萬兩。
units.en: Repairs proceeding in sequence would cost roughly five or six hundred thousand taels.
units.literal: Repair work proceeding in sequence would require enormous costs—approximately five or six hundred thousand taels of silver.

units.zh: 此項巨費，即盡括商股餘利息項，亦難支抵。
units.en: Even pooling all remaining merchant share dividends would not cover this enormous expense.
units.literal: This enormous expense—even pooling all remaining merchant share interest—would be difficult to cover.

units.zh: 此大修之宜歸官辦者也。
units.en: This is why major repairs should fall under government operation.
units.literal: This is why major repairs should be placed under government operation.

units.zh: 中國報費昂貴，甲於全球。
units.en: China's telegram fees are the highest in the world.
units.literal: China's telegram fees are expensive, ranking first globally.

units.zh: 遠省一二字之費，幾與各國二十字相等。
units.en: In remote provinces, the fee for one or two characters nearly equals twenty characters elsewhere.
units.literal: In remote provinces, the fee for one or two characters is nearly equal to twenty characters in other countries.

units.zh: 近據寧夏副都統志銳，請核減報費以利交通。
units.en: Recently, Zhi Rui, Deputy Commander of Ningxia, requested a reduction in telegram fees to improve communications.
units.literal: Recently, according to the Deputy Commander of Ningxia Zhi Rui, a request was made to reduce telegram fees to benefit communications.

units.zh: 又據赴葡部員周萬鵬稱，葡國公會亦以中國報費太昂為詞。
units.en: Zhou Wanpeng, an official sent to Portugal, also reported that the Portuguese assembly cited China's excessively high telegram fees.
units.literal: Also according to Zhou Wanpeng, an official sent to Portugal, the Portuguese assembly likewise cited China's excessively high telegram fees.

units.zh: 自當酌減，使價目與各國略同，為入萬國電政會之預備。
units.en: Fees should be reduced to bring prices in line with other countries, as preparation for joining the international telegraph union.
units.literal: Fees should be appropriately reduced so that prices approximate those of other countries, as preparation for joining the international telegraph union.

units.zh: 惟核減電費，以歲入三百餘萬元計算，若減一二成，即在五六十萬以上。
units.en: However, with annual revenue exceeding three million yuan, a ten- or twenty-percent fee reduction would cost five or six hundred thousand yuan or more.
units.literal: However, reducing telegraph fees—calculated on annual revenue of over three million yuan—a reduction of ten or twenty percent would amount to over five or six hundred thousand.

units.zh: 若遞減至四五成，或減至與東西洋相等，為數尤多。
units.en: A progressive reduction to forty or fifty percent, or matching Western rates, would cost even more.
units.literal: If reduced progressively to forty or fifty percent, or reduced to match East and West, the amount would be even greater.

units.zh: 此事一行，則商股年息恐不可保，餘利更不待言。
units.en: Once implemented, annual dividends on merchant shares would likely become unsustainable—not to mention any remaining profits.
units.literal: Once this is implemented, annual dividends on merchant shares would likely be unsustainable, to say nothing of remaining profits.

units.zh: 此減費之宜歸官辦者也。
units.en: This is why fee reduction should fall under government operation.
units.literal: This is why fee reduction should be placed under government operation.

units.zh: 凡此三事，實為電政今日最要之圖，即為商股今日最損之策。
units.en: These three matters are the telegraph administration's most urgent priorities—and the most damaging policies for merchant shareholders.
units.literal: These three matters are truly the most important projects for telegraph administration today, and the most damaging policies for merchant shares today.

units.zh: 與其苟且因循，日積月累，致官商之兩病，曷若平價收贖，期上下之交益。
units.en: Rather than muddling through and harming both government and merchants, it is better to buy out shares at fair prices and restore mutual trust.
units.literal: Rather than muddling through day by day and month by month, causing illness for both government and merchants, it is better to buy out shares at fair prices and seek mutual benefit between superiors and subordinates.

units.zh: 實見夫今日電報有必須擴充之勢，即有不免折閱之時。
units.en: Telegraphy must expand today, even if losses are inevitable at times.
units.literal: It is clear that telegraphy today must expand, even if there are inevitably times of loss.

units.zh: 在商人祗課贏餘，在國家必求利便。
units.en: Merchants seek profit; the state must seek public convenience.
units.literal: Merchants seek only surplus profit; the state must seek convenience and benefit.

units.zh: 事實不同，斷難強合。
units.en: Their interests diverge—they cannot be forcibly combined.
units.literal: The facts differ—they cannot be forcibly combined.

units.zh: 臣等擬恪遵光緒二十八年諭旨，改為官辦，籌還商股。
units.en: We propose to follow the 1902 edict, converting to government operation and repurchasing merchant shares.
units.literal: We propose to faithfully follow the edict of the twenty-eighth year of Guangxu, changing to government operation and arranging repayment of merchant shares.

units.zh: 即由部備價收贖，於每股股本外特予加價，以示國家恤商之意。」
units.en: The ministry will buy out shares at a premium above par value to show the state's regard for merchants."
units.literal: The ministry will prepare funds to buy out shares, granting a premium above par value to show the state's care for merchants."

units.zh: 奏入，允行。
units.en: The memorial was submitted and approved.
units.literal: The memorial was submitted and approved.

units.zh: 八月，電股收贖完竣。
units.en: In August, the buyout of telegraph shares was completed.
units.literal: In the eighth month, the buyout of telegraph shares was completed.

units.zh: 陳璧疏言：「臣部收贖商電，酌核市值贖之，每百圓電股，給予一百七十圓。
units.en: Chen Bi reported: "Our ministry bought out merchant telegraph shares at assessed market value, paying 170 yuan for every 100-yuan share.
units.literal: Chen Bi memorialized: "Our ministry bought out merchant telegraph shares after assessing market value, paying one hundred seventy yuan for every hundred-yuan telegraph share.

units.zh: 旋復從眾商之請，加價十圓，作為優待費。
units.en: At merchants' request, an additional ten yuan was added as a preferential bonus.
units.literal: Subsequently, acceding to merchants' request, an additional ten yuan was added as a preferential bonus.

units.zh: 計共二十二萬圓。
units.en: The total bonus amounted to 220,000 yuan.
units.literal: The total amounted to two hundred twenty thousand yuan.

units.zh: 自頒發收贖章程後，旬月之間，共收回商股二萬一千四百餘股。
units.en: Within six weeks of issuing buyout regulations, over 21,400 merchant shares were recovered.
units.literal: From the issuance of buyout regulations, within a month and ten days, over twenty-one thousand four hundred merchant shares were recovered.

units.zh: 其未到之五百餘股，委系外埠及內地僻處，遞寄維艱，擬請寬予限期，照章給價，提存現款，以便續領，仍給優待費，以示體恤。
units.en: The remaining 500-odd shares are held in remote ports and interior regions where delivery is difficult. We propose extending the deadline, paying according to regulations, holding cash in deposit for later collection, and still granting the preferential bonus.
units.literal: The remaining five hundred odd shares not yet submitted are held in remote ports and interior regions where delivery is difficult. We propose extending the deadline, paying according to regulations, holding cash in deposit for later collection, and still granting the preferential bonus to show consideration.

units.zh: 此後即全歸國有，與商無涉。
units.en: Thereafter the telegraph would be entirely state-owned, with no further merchant involvement.
units.literal: Thereafter it would be entirely state-owned, with no further merchant involvement.

units.zh: 收贖之款三百九十六萬，臣部暫由路款借撥，仍須另行設法歸還，以清款目。」
units.en: The 3.96 million yuan buyout was temporarily advanced from railway funds and must be repaid through other means to settle accounts."
units.literal: The buyout funds of three million nine hundred sixty thousand were temporarily advanced from railway funds by our ministry, but must be repaid by other means to settle accounts."

units.zh: 又言：「電政為交通樞機，圖擴充方期發達。
units.en: He also argued: "Telegraph administration is the pivot of communications; only through expansion can it develop.
units.literal: He also stated: "Telegraph administration is the pivot of communications; only through planned expansion can development be expected.

units.zh: 今既改歸國有，應將減費、展線、修線諸事次第整頓。
units.en: Now that it is state-owned, fee reduction, line expansion, and repairs should be systematically reorganized.
units.literal: Now that it has been converted to state ownership, fee reduction, line expansion, and line repair should be systematically reorganized in sequence.

units.zh: 而減價為中外眾目所睹，非實行籌辦，尤不足以饜人望而廣招徠。
units.en: Fee reduction is watched by Chinese and foreign observers alike. Without actual implementation, it would not satisfy public expectations or attract broader use.
units.literal: Fee reduction is watched by Chinese and foreign observers alike. Without actual implementation and planning, it would not satisfy public expectations or broadly attract business.

units.zh: 擬自光緒三十五年正月始，酌減電費二成，以所收商報約三百萬圓之額計之，即少收約六十萬圓，不敷在二十萬圓以上。
units.en: A twenty-percent fee reduction is proposed beginning January 1909. Based on commercial telegram revenue of roughly three million yuan, this would reduce income by approximately six hundred thousand yuan—a shortfall exceeding two hundred thousand yuan.
units.literal: It is proposed to reduce telegraph fees by twenty percent beginning the first month of the thirty-fifth year of Guangxu. Calculated on commercial telegram revenue of approximately three million yuan, this would reduce income by approximately six hundred thousand yuan—a shortfall exceeding two hundred thousand yuan.

units.zh: 減費之後，報費必增，可供挹注。
units.en: After fee reduction, increased traffic should provide supplementary revenue.
units.literal: After fee reduction, telegram traffic will surely increase, providing supplementary revenue.

units.zh: 而一時添線、修線，並擴充電話，在在需款。
units.en: Meanwhile, adding lines, repairing lines, and expanding telephone service all require funds.
units.literal: Meanwhile, adding lines, repairing lines, and expanding telephone service all require funds everywhere.

units.zh: 所增之數，必須抵撥，逐漸推廣工程之用。
units.en: Increased revenue must be allocated to fund expansion projects gradually.
units.literal: Increased revenue must be allocated to gradually fund expansion projects.

units.zh: 預算短額，擬暫由臣部各路餘利項下，每年分撥二十萬圓，以三年為限，自第四年起至六年止，每年勻還二十萬圓，一律還清。
units.en: For the projected shortfall, 200,000 yuan annually would be temporarily allocated from railway surplus profits for three years, then repaid at 200,000 yuan per year from years four through six until fully settled.
units.literal: For the projected shortfall, it is proposed to temporarily allocate two hundred thousand yuan annually from our ministry's railway surplus profits for three years, then repay two hundred thousand yuan annually from the fourth through sixth years until fully repaid.

units.zh: 一轉移間，路款均歸有著，電政亦可漸興，不煩續借他款，實收財政統籌之益。」
units.en: With this transfer, railway funds would be properly accounted for, telegraph administration could gradually prosper, and no further borrowing would be needed—a genuine benefit of fiscal coordination."
units.literal: With this transfer, railway funds would be properly accounted for, telegraph administration could gradually prosper, and no further borrowing would be needed—truly achieving the benefits of fiscal coordination."

units.zh: 報可。
units.en: The report was approved.
units.literal: The report was approved.

units.zh: 自時厥後，事權統一，呼應靈通，每歲展拓電線三四千里以為常。
units.en: From that point on, with unified authority and swift coordination, expanding telegraph lines by three or four thousand li annually became routine.
units.literal: From that time onward, authority was unified and coordination swift. Expanding telegraph lines by three or four thousand li each year became routine.

units.zh: 而取值之廉，迥異疇昔，此則非商辦之所及也。
units.en: Low fees, vastly different from before, were something merchant operation could never have achieved.
units.literal: And the low fees were vastly different from before—something merchant operation could not achieve.

units.zh: 中國幅員遼闊，文報稽延，至於變起倉猝，往往因消息遲滯，坐誤機宜，釀成鉅患。
units.en: China's vast territory made official dispatches slow. When sudden crises arose, delayed intelligence often caused missed opportunities and bred great calamity.
units.literal: China's territory is vast and official dispatches are delayed. When sudden disturbances arise, delayed news often causes missed opportunities and breeds great calamity.

units.zh: 歷朝變亂之起，大率以此。
units.en: Rebellions throughout history have largely begun for this reason.
units.literal: Rebellions throughout history have largely begun for this reason.

units.zh: 自有電報，舉向來音信隔絕之弊，一掃而空。
units.en: Telegraphy swept away the longstanding problem of cut-off communications.
units.literal: Since telegraphy was established, the longstanding evil of cut-off communications has been swept away entirely.

units.zh: 若朝陽教匪之倡亂，雲南猛喇游匪魏名高之滋事，均因電報之告警，與軍事布置之迅速，得以立即剿平。
units.en: The sectarian uprising in Chaoyang and the roving bandit Wei Minggao's disturbances in Mengla, Yunnan were both suppressed immediately thanks to telegraph alerts and rapid military deployment.
units.literal: The sectarian uprising in Chaoyang and the roving bandit Wei Minggao's disturbances in Mengla, Yunnan were both suppressed immediately thanks to telegraph alarms and rapid military deployment.

units.zh: 而外則朝鮮之二次內訌，越南事變之先事防禦，亦惟電報是賴。
units.en: Abroad, Korea's second internal conflict and advance defense against disturbances in Vietnam also relied solely on the telegraph.
units.literal: Abroad, the second internal conflict in Korea and advance defense against disturbances in Vietnam also relied solely on the telegraph.

units.zh: 此其明效大驗也。
units.en: These were clear and decisive proofs of its value.
units.literal: These are its clear and great proofs of effectiveness.

units.zh: 而然當創辦之初，鄉僻囿於見聞，外人多所撓阻，艱難曲折，乃克成功。
units.en: Yet at its founding, remote regions were ignorant of the technology, foreigners obstructed at every turn, and success came only through hardship.
units.literal: Yet at its founding, remote regions were confined by limited knowledge, foreigners obstructed in many ways, and success came only through hardship and difficulty.

units.zh: 設線之處，若系邊疆瘴癘、塞外荒涼之地，措手之艱，什伯內地。
units.en: Installing lines in frontier malarial regions or desolate lands beyond the frontier was ten or a hundred times harder than in the interior.
units.literal: Where lines were installed in frontier malarial regions or desolate lands beyond the frontier, the difficulty of execution was ten or a hundred times that of the interior.

units.zh: 以故在事人員，得邀獎敘，而近省不得援例以請者此也。
units.en: Personnel involved received commendations and promotions, while those in nearby provinces could not cite precedent to request the same.
units.literal: Therefore personnel involved received commendations and promotions, while those in nearby provinces could not cite precedent to request the same—for this reason.

units.zh: 至於意外之損壞，其事尤夥。
units.en: Accidental damage, meanwhile, was especially frequent.
units.literal: As for accidental damage, such incidents were especially numerous.

units.zh: 貴州畢節鄉民之拆線；
units.en: Villagers in Bijie, Guizhou, dismantled lines;
units.literal: Villagers in Bijie, Guizhou dismantled lines;

units.zh: 山西霍山鄉民之毀桿；
units.en: villagers in Huoshan, Shanxi, destroyed poles;
units.literal: villagers in Huoshan, Shanxi destroyed poles;

units.zh: 湘省澧州民誤以電線為外人所設，集眾毀棄；
units.en: people in Lizhou, Hunan, mistaking the lines for foreign installations, gathered to destroy them;
units.literal: people in Lizhou, Hunan, mistaking the lines for foreign installations, gathered to destroy them;

units.zh: 陝之長武、乾州、醴泉、邠州、永壽，甘之涇州、平涼等處，人民謂旱疫為電線所致，拆毀殆盡。
units.en: in Changwu, Qianzhou, Liquan, Binzhou, and Yongshou in Shaanxi, and Jingzhou, Pingliang, and elsewhere in Gansu, people blamed drought and plague on telegraph lines and destroyed them almost entirely.
units.literal: in Changwu, Qianzhou, Liquan, Binzhou, and Yongshou in Shaanxi, and Jingzhou, Pingliang, and other places in Gansu, people believed drought and plague were caused by telegraph lines and destroyed them nearly completely.

units.zh: 俱由地方官出貲修復，首犯有論重辟者。
units.en: Local officials paid for repairs in all cases, and ringleaders received severe punishment.
units.literal: Local officials paid for repairs in all cases, and ringleaders received severe punishment.

units.zh: 二十六年拳匪之變，京師至保定電線先為所毀，京津、京德繼之，山西、河南又繼之。
units.en: During the 1900 Boxer uprising, the Beijing-Baoding line was destroyed first, followed by the Beijing-Tianjin and Beijing-Dezhou lines, then Shanxi and Henan.
units.literal: During the Boxer uprising in the twenty-sixth year, the Beijing-Baoding line was first destroyed, followed by Beijing-Tianjin and Beijing-Dezhou lines, then Shanxi and Henan.

units.zh: 馴至晉、豫、直隸、山東四省境內，蕩然無一線之遺。
units.en: Eventually not a single line remained in Shanxi, Henan, Zhili, and Shandong.
units.literal: Eventually within Shanxi, Henan, Zhili, and Shandong, not a single line remained.

units.zh: 南北隔閡，中外阻塞，消息不通者數月。
units.en: North and south were cut off, domestic and foreign communications blocked, for months.
units.literal: North and south were cut off, Chinese and foreign communications blocked, with no news for months.

units.zh: 而外兵盤踞京、津，初設行軍電線，嗣擬設大沽至上海水線，以大東、大北兩公司主其事。
units.en: Meanwhile foreign troops occupied Beijing and Tianjin, installing field telegraph lines and planning a Dagu-Shanghai submarine cable through the Eastern Extension and Great Northern companies.
units.literal: Meanwhile foreign troops occupied Beijing and Tianjin, first installing field telegraph lines, then planning a Dagu-Shanghai submarine cable to be managed by the Eastern Extension and Great Northern companies.

units.zh: 宣懷密行作價，購其機器料物，屬於中國商局，其謀竟不得逞。
units.en: Sheng Xuanhuai secretly negotiated to purchase their equipment for the Chinese merchant bureau, and their scheme failed.
units.literal: Sheng Xuanhuai secretly negotiated a price and purchased their equipment and materials for the Chinese merchant bureau, and their scheme ultimately failed.

units.zh: 宣懷尋請修復已毀各線。
units.en: Sheng Xuanhuai soon petitioned to repair all destroyed lines.
units.literal: Sheng Xuanhuai soon requested repair of all destroyed lines.

units.zh: 其經戰事損壞者，商局任之。
units.en: Lines damaged by warfare were the merchant bureau's responsibility.
units.literal: Lines damaged by warfare were the merchant bureau's responsibility.

units.zh: 晉、豫未有戰事，地方官保護不力，甚且指使拆壞者，援畢節、霍山之例，分別賠修。
units.en: Shanxi and Henan saw no warfare, but local officials failed to protect lines and even directed destroyers. Following the Bijie and Huoshan precedents, they were required to pay for repairs.
units.literal: Shanxi and Henan saw no warfare, but local officials failed to protect lines and even directed destroyers. Following the Bijie and Huoshan precedents, they were respectively required to pay for repairs.

units.zh: 報可。
units.en: The report was approved.
units.literal: The report was approved.

units.zh: 三十年，東三省線再毀於日俄之戰。
units.en: In 1904, the Three Eastern Provinces' lines were again destroyed in the Russo-Japanese War.
units.literal: In the thirtieth year, the Three Eastern Provinces' lines were again destroyed in the Russo-Japanese War.

units.zh: 迨三十四年，總督徐世昌修復之。
units.en: By 1908, Governor-General Xu Shichang had restored them.
